summary: Tested the new real-time notification feature end-to-end (backend + frontend). Created /app/backend/tests/test_notifications_sms.py (23 tests, 21 pass): dev-mode SMS outbox flow (assigned -> out_for_delivery -> arriving -> delivered with /confirm link, each sent exactly once, all bodies end 'Reply STOP to opt out.', status dev_outbox, twilio_configured=false), CASL (zero SMS for a no-consent job at every stage), STOP/START Twilio webhook + blocked_optout on subsequent send, admin SMS outbox/opt-out endpoints incl. RBAC + 422 validation, public /api/public/confirm/{token} GET+POST (rating creates one review titled 'Delivery recipient', second POST returns rating_saved=false, bad token 404, facility owner gets recipient_confirmed), notifications list/read (all + ids), per-user isolation, facility lifecycle notifications, driver-cancel/staff-cancel dispatcher alerts and stale_job dedupe. Frontend verified with Playwright: NotificationBell on /admin, /dispatch (dark), facility portal, driver /dashboard and /jobs (panel opens, items render, mark-all-read clears badge), Admin Compliance SMS outbox table + 'Dev mode' badge + opt-out add/remove, facility CASL consent checkbox (booking persisted recipient_sms_consent=true), driver arriving-soon button (toast 'Recipient notified by SMS' + disables), public /confirm/{token} page (stars, comment, thank-you, revisit thank-you, invalid token error). Regression: all existing pytest suites pass except 2 pre-existing failures. Cleaned all TEST_ jobs/notifications/outbox rows and restored driver1/facility1 to no-active-job state.

critical.issue: Driver receives NO job_offer in-app notification in the main dispatch flow. Facility bookings are created with status 'offered' (POST /api/facility/requests, server.py ~3138) while assigned_driver_id is null, so when a dispatcher later assigns a driver the status does not change and the 'if new_status and new_status != job.status' guard (server.py ~2426) skips notify_user. Verified: assigning driver1 to a fresh facility-booked job produced 0 notifications; the same job moved to 'open' first and then offered does notify. Fix: fire job_offer whenever assigned_driver_id changes (or create facility requests with status 'open').

minor.issue: Two notifications per return for dispatchers: legacy notify_job_return() writes a doc with only a 'message' field (no title/body) plus the new notify_dispatchers('job_returned') doc. The legacy doc renders as an empty row in NotificationBell (it reads n.title/n.body). 16 such title-less docs existed in db.notifications. Remove notify_job_return() or migrate it to notify_user().

Route is declared twice (server.py 2684 and 3837); the first declaration wins, so the ?limit param is ignored and 'unread' is computed only from the newest 50 rows (undercounts when more than 50 unread). Delete the older duplicate.

Pre-existing regression failure tests/test_driver_available_jobs.py::TestAvailableMasking::test_only_open_or_offered_to_me — facility-booked jobs appear with status 'offered' and assigned_driver_id null, violating the offer semantics (same root cause as the HIGH issue above).

Pre-existing: no brute-force lockout — 6 consecutive wrong passwords all return 401 and the valid login still succeeds (tests/test_auth_hardening.py::test_brute_force_lockout_after_5_failures fails). Playbook expects 423/429 after 5 failures.

Pre-existing: CORSMiddleware uses allow_credentials=True with CORS_ORIGINS="*" (backend/.env) — browsers reject credentialed wildcard origins; and login returns a bearer token only (no httpOnly cookie), so the playbook cookie requirement is unmet.

ui_bugs.issue: Legacy title-less job_returned notifications render as blank rows (title/body undefined) — data-side bug listed above; UI should also guard with n.title || n.message fallback

rca_of_the_issue: Job-offer notifications hinge on a status transition ('if new_status and new_status != job.status'). Because POST /api/facility/requests inserts jobs already in status 'offered' with no driver, a dispatcher assigning a driver produces no status change and therefore no notify_user() call, so drivers never see the offer in the bell. Separately, the 'returned' custody event calls both the legacy notify_job_return() (writes a 'message'-only doc) and the new notify_dispatchers(), producing a duplicate plus a blank-rendering notification.
